script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SMALL TOWN - DAY

A quaint, small town nestled between the hills and the sea. Rolling green hills extend towards the horizon, dotted with farmhouses. The salty sea breeze carries the sounds of cawing seagulls and distant laughter.

INT. FARMHOUSE KITCHEN - MORNING

SARAH, 35, a warm and kind farmer's wife, prepares breakfast as her husband, MIKE, 38, enters the kitchen. He wears overalls and has a rugged farmer's tan.

MIKE: (Smiling) Mornin', love.

SARAH: (Smiling back) Morning, Mike.

MIKE: Did you hear about Mr. Thompson? He's quitting the post office.

SARAH: (Frowning) Really? Why?

MIKE: Retirement, I guess. He mentioned something about wanting to travel the world.

SARAH: That's nice. He deserves it.

MIKE: (Nods) I suppose so. But now they're looking for someone to replace him.

SARAH: (Pauses) I've always thought about applying.

MIKE: (Surprised) Have you, now?

SARAH: (Nervously) Well, just for the experience. It might be nice to get out of the house for a few hours.

MIKE: (Gently) You'd be great at it, love. Go ahead and apply.

INT. POST OFFICE - DAY

SARAH sits across from an INTERVIEWER, 50s, who sits behind a large desk.

INTERVIEWER: So, Sarah, tell me about yourself.

SARAH: (Nervously) I'm Sarah. I live in this small town, and I've been married to Mike for 10 years. We run a small farm, and I've been helping out at the post office when they're short-staffed.

INTERVIEWER: (Impressed) That's impressive. Why do you want to work here full-time?

SARAH: (Confidently) I enjoy the social interaction and the sense of community it brings. I think it would be a nice change of pace from farm life.

INT. FARMHOUSE LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Mike, Sarah, and their teenage daughter, EMMA, sit around the dinner table.

EMMA: (Excitedly) Mom! I heard you got the job!

SARAH: (Smiling) Yes, I did. Starting next week.

MIKE: (Proudly) That's great news, Sarah.

EMMA: (Curiously) What will you be doing?

SARAH: (Smiling) Sorting mail, selling stamps, and helping customers.

EMMA: That sounds boring.

SARAH: (Chuckles) Sometimes it can be, but it's part of the small-town charm.

INT. POST OFFICE - DAY

First day on the job. Sarah is nervous but determined. She greets regulars with a warm smile and sorts mail efficiently.

A NEW FACE, JASON, 20s, enters the post office. He's a newcomer to the town and looks unsure.

SARAH: (Friendly) Hi there. Welcome to our little post office. How may I help you today?

JASON: (Surprised) Wow. You're new. I haven't seen you here before.

SARAH: (Smiling) Yes, I started a few days ago. What can I help you with?

JASON: (Relieved) Oh, just need to send a package.

As Sarah helps him, they strike up a conversation, discovering they have a lot in common. By the end of the day, Sarah feels a renewed sense of purpose and joy.

INT. SMALL TOWN BAR - NIGHT

Sarah, Mike, and Emma sit at a table, enjoying a night out together.

EMMA: (Teasingly) So, how's the new job?

SARAH: (Laughing) It's going well. I've met some interesting people, like Jason.

MIKE: (Raising an eyebrow) Oh? What's so interesting about him?

SARAH: (Smiling) He's new to the town and we've got a lot in common.

MIKE: (Grinning) That's nice. Maybe you'll have a new friend.

Sarah smiles, feeling a sense of excitement for her new journey in the small town.

FADE OUT.
